firstRun.title: Before you start
firstRun.p1: Schengen Guard is a personal trip-tracking tool, not immigration or legal advice. Its 90/180-day calculations are provided for informational purposes only, with no warranty of accuracy. Always verify borderline cases against the European Commission's official short-stay calculator and with the relevant border authority or consulate before you travel.
firstRun.p2: All your trip data stays on this device only — nothing is sent anywhere. See Settings → Privacy & Terms for details.
home.disclaimerFooter: Not legal advice — verify with the official EU calculator

faq.heading: FAQ & terms
faq.dataPrivacy.title: Data & privacy
faq.dataStored.a: On this device only, in your browser's local storage. There's no account and no server — nothing about your trips is ever sent anywhere.
faq.internet.q: Do I need an internet connection?
faq.internet.a: No. Once the app is open, it works fully offline — logging stays, checking dates, and calculating your 90/180 status all happen entirely on your device.
faq.backup.title: Backup
faq.lostPhone.q: What happens if I lose my phone or clear my browser data?
faq.lostPhone.a: Your trip data is gone unless you exported a backup first. There's no server copy to restore from — that's the trade-off for keeping your data private, but it means backing up is entirely on you.
faq.backupHow.q: How do I back up or move my data to a new device?
faq.backupHow.a: Go to Settings → Backup & restore → "Back up my trips" to download a JSON file. On your new device (or after reinstalling), use "Restore from backup" to load it back in.
faq.rollingPeriod.a: It means the 180-day window that counts toward your limit isn't fixed to the calendar — it moves with you. On any given day, the app looks back at the previous 180 days and adds up how many of them you spent in Schengen. As days roll out of that window, they stop counting, even if you never left. That's why your days-left number can go up over time on its own — you're not spending down a fixed allowance, you're always looking at a fresh 180-day slice ending today.
faq.dayCounts.q: What counts as a day in the Schengen Area?
faq.dayCounts.a: Any calendar day you're physically present in the Schengen Area counts as a full day — including your entry and exit days, even if you only cross the border for an hour.
faq.howCalculated.q: How is the 90/180 rule actually calculated?
faq.howCalculated.a: The app looks at a rolling 180-day window ending on any given date and counts how many of those days you spent in Schengen. If that count goes over 90, you're over the limit. Tap "How is this calculated?" on Home or the Safe Trip Checker to see the day-by-day math behind any number.
faq.sideTrips.q: Do side trips outside Schengen (UK, etc.) count?
faq.sideTrips.a: No. If part of a longer trip takes you outside the Schengen Area — a UK leg, for example — mark those days as excluded when logging the stay in Calendar, and they won't count toward your 90-day total.
faq.exportVisa.q: How do I export my trip history for a visa application?
faq.exportVisa.a: Go to Settings → Export trip history. "Export as CSV" gives you a spreadsheet-friendly file; "Print / save as PDF" gives you a formatted summary to hand to a border official or include with a visa application. Neither is the same as the JSON backup — use Backup & restore for that.
faq.etias.q: What is ETIAS, and does it affect my 90/180-day count?
faq.etias.a1: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is a separate travel authorization, not a visa. Starting late 2026, most visitors from visa-exempt countries — including the US, UK, and Canada — will need to apply for one online before traveling to the Schengen Area.
faq.etias.a2: Here's the part that matters for this app: ETIAS doesn't change the 90/180 rule. It's a pre-travel authorization step layered on top of the existing rule, not a replacement for it. Once you're approved, your stay is still governed by the same 90-days-in-any-180-day-window limit this app tracks. Getting ETIAS approved doesn't extend your allowed days, and it doesn't reset your count.
faq.etias.a3: ETIAS applications aren't handled through this app — apply directly at the official EU site. This page is here to explain how it fits with your day count, not to process your application.
faq.etias.lastChecked: Last checked: {{date}}. ETIAS's launch date has shifted before, so treat the timing above as current-best-information rather than fixed — check {{link}} for the authoritative date.
faq.disclaimer.notAdvice: Schengen Guard is a personal tracking tool, not immigration or legal advice.
faq.disclaimer.verify: You're responsible for independently verifying your own compliance before you travel — the app's calculations are a best-effort aid, not a guarantee.
faq.disclaimer.liability: We accept no liability for overstay consequences based on the app's output.
faq.disclaimer.dataLoss: Trip data lives only on this device. It is not recoverable by the app or its developer if the device is lost, the app is uninstalled, or browser data is cleared — exporting a backup is your own responsibility.

privacy.heading: Privacy & Terms
privacy.notice.1: No account, no sign-in, no server, no network calls of any kind.
privacy.notice.2: Trip data, notification preferences, and theme choice are stored only in this browser's local storage on this device.
privacy.notice.3: Nothing is transmitted to the developer or any third party. There is no analytics, tracking, or advertising in this app.
privacy.notice.4: Local storage is used solely to run the app's own features (saving trips, remembering your theme and notification settings) — never for tracking.
privacy.notice.5: Export, Import, and "Clear all logged stays" (Settings → Data) are the only ways your data moves off, into, or out of this device.
privacy.notice.ios: iOS note: if you don't open the app for roughly a week or more, iOS may automatically clear locally stored website/app data as part of its normal storage-management behaviour. Export a backup periodically if you want to keep your trip history safe.
privacy.terms.1: Schengen Guard is provided "as is," for informational and personal record-keeping purposes only.
privacy.terms.2: It is not immigration, legal, or professional advice, and no warranty is made as to the accuracy, completeness, or fitness of its calculations for any particular purpose.
privacy.terms.3: You are responsible for independently verifying your compliance with the 90/180-day rule (or any other entry requirement) using official sources — the European Commission's short-stay calculator, the border authority of the country you're visiting, or a qualified immigration professional — particularly for any borderline case.
privacy.terms.4: To the fullest extent permitted by law, the developer disclaims liability for any loss or damage arising from reliance on the app's output, including missed flights, denied entry, fines, or other immigration consequences.
